elements.text: If patient just had a seizure 20.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: If new sudden asymmetric weakness or numbness of face/arm/leg, difficulty speaking or visual disturbance, consider stroke or TIA 152.

elements.text: If recent head injury 30.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: If suicidal thoughts or plans 34.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: If difficulty breathing, respiratory rate > 30, oxygen saturation < 94% or oxygen saturation machine not available, give face mask oxygen.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Check glucose: if < 3 (or < 4 if diabetes) or ≥ 11.1 19.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: If thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor, sunken eyes, decreased urine, give oral rehydration solution. If unable to drink or BP < 90/60, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until systolic BP > 90. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Consider involuntary admission if signs of mental illness and refuses treatment/admission and a danger to self, others, own reputation or financial interest/property 158.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: If HIV positive with recent positive cryptococcal antigen test, refer for urgent lumbar puncture (LP).

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Look for delirium, mania, psychosis, intoxication, withdrawal or poisoning and manage before referral:

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Varying levels of consciousness over hours/days and temperature ≥ 38°C

elements.section: Manage urgently:

elements.text: Refer urgently unless:

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Patient with known schizophrenia who is otherwise well, give routine schizophrenia care 162.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Patient with diabetes and low glucose on insulin. If abnormal thoughts/behaviour resolves with dextrose, no need to refer, give routine diabetes care 145.

elements.section: Manage urgently:
elements.text: Patient with known alcohol use who is otherwise well. If abnormal thoughts/behaviour resolves once sober, no need to refer 165.
ABNORMAL THOUGHTS OR BEHAVIOUR

Approach to the patient with abnormal thoughts or behaviour not needing urgent attention • If for at least 6 months ≥ 1 of: memory problems, disorientation, language difficulty, less able to cope with daily activities and work/social function, consider dementia 166. • If unsure of diagnosis, refer for further assessment.

1If severe penicillin allergy (previous angioedema, anaphylaxis or urticaria), discuss with doctor. Do not mix Ringer's lactate and IV ceftriaxone. 2Stimulants include: methamphetamines (tik), cocaine (crack), methaqualone (mandrax), cannabis.
